text:
maya (support): customer reports function/tool call failing in JSON mode; they see 'Invalid function arguments: missing required key \"order_items\"' even though payload includes order_items. ticket: #C-8842

alex (support): can you paste the exact request body and the error response? also customer org id and model they hit?

support-bot: New escalation created: #C-8842 - severity: high - tagged: @eng-ml @eng-runtime

maya (support): customer org: acme-retail-22, model: gptx-4f-infer (pinned). here's excerpt from their client (redacted):
```json
{
  "input": "Create order for user 123",
  "json_mode": true,
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "create_order",
      "arguments_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["order_id","order_items"],
        "properties": {"order_id": {"type":"string"}, "order_items": {"type":"array"}}
    },
    "call": {
      "order_id": "ord-9292",
      "order_items": "[{\"sku\":\"X12\",\"qty\":1}]"
    }
  ]
}
```

maya (support): note: order_items looks like an array in their schema but they send it as a JSON-encoded string. server returns 400: \"Invalid function arguments: expected array for order_items, got string\"

jordan (eng-ml): thanks. this matches earlier incidents where customers accidentally double-encode nested JSON when using templated prompts or older SDKs. is the customer using our JS client or calling REST directly?

maya (support): they call our REST endpoint directly from a Java-based backend. they said they used String.valueOf(items) before sending.

sam (eng-runtime): can we get the raw request/headers from the logs? need to verify content-type and whether we performed any auto-coercion. tagging @ops-oncall for log access.

ops-oncall: pulled logs for org acme-retail-22 around ts=1965432050-1965432200. raw request body matches the payload above. content-type: application/json. no middleware transformations observed.

alex (support): suggested repro steps to customer: 1) send order_items as actual JSON array (no escaping), 2) try a direct curl repro, 3) if using SDK older than 2.5.1 upgrade. can we provide a curl they can run?

jordan (eng-ml): please include this simple curl repro in the reply so they can confirm:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input":"Create order","json_mode":true,"functions":[{"name":"create_order","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","required":["order_id","order_items"],"properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"order_items":{"type":"array"}}},"call":{"order_id":"ord-9292","order_items":[{"sku":"X12","qty":1}]}}]}'
```

maya (support): customer tried that and says still failing but with different msg: \"JSON parsing error: unexpected token at position 215\". they attached model response token log (snippet):
```
...\"create_order\": \"{\\\"order_id\\\":\\\"ord-9292\\\",\\\"order_items\\\": \\\"[{\\\\\\\"sku\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"X12\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"qty\\\\\\\":1}]\\\"}\"...
```

jordan (eng-ml): that token log shows the model produced a string for order_items. likely prompt/template encourages the model to emit serialized JSON string. when JSON mode enforces schema, runtime tries to parse produced value as array and fails. we need to know if the model candidate is returning string-encoded JSON instead of native arrays. which generation variant was used? streaming or non-streaming?

maya (support): streaming response parameter was true. customer says they used a template with an example where order_items was printed as a string.

sam (eng-runtime): two action items: 1) provide customer-facing troubleshooting steps, 2) add a quick runtime guard that attempts to JSON.parse values for top-level function fields when types mismatch and accepts if parse succeeds (with a warning) to reduce friction. I'll file an issue.

jordan (eng-ml): agree on guard + warning. for short term, advise customer to change examples in prompt and to set streaming=false to see full generated JSON; streaming sometimes truncates tokens that help the model close arrays. also suggest using our 'structured_output.strict=false' flag if they want tolerant parsing (note: this relaxes enforcement).

alex (support): drafting reply to customer: 1) confirm they should send order_items as array, 2) if model emits stringified array, ask them to try setting streaming=false or set structured_output.strict=false as a temporary workaround, 3) share curl repro above and ask for full server logs if still failing.

maya (support): customer replied they can switch to non-streaming repro, will try and get back.

ops-oncall: created issue R-INF-4021 in eng-runtime: \"tolerant coercion for function arg types where value is JSON-encoded string\" and assigned to sam. jira link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/R-INF-4021

sam (eng-runtime): assigned, will prioritize P2. quick patch: if a field is declared array/object and runtime sees a string, attempt JSON.parse up to 2 levels deep and accept on success while logging a warning and incrementing a metric (func_arg_coercion).

jordan (eng-ml): also adding a test in our evals repo to ensure models don't output serialized strings for array fields when given clear examples.

alex (support): thanks team. maya will follow up with customer when they finish repro steps. :thumbsup:

maya (support): marking thread resolved until customer confirms. will reopen if repro persists. :white_check_mark:
